subject: BridgeCare discovery — private/VPC deployment playbook (recap & next steps)
messages:
From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@bridgecarehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:35:00 -0500
Subject: BridgeCare discovery — private/VPC deployment playbook (recap & next steps)

Hi Dana / Karen,

Thanks again for taking the time earlier — helpful conversation. This note captures what we heard, success criteria you outlined, and suggested next steps so we’re aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points (as described):
- Regulatory constraints: PHI residency in US, need audit-grade logging and SOC2-compatible controls.
- Key management: must support customer-managed keys (CMEK), and potential HSM-backed KMS.
- Network posture: air-gapped option for isolated sites; primary preference is VPC with strict egress controls and IP allowlists.
- Integration: BridgeCare currently runs inference calls from an on-prem orchestration layer (K8s + Istio) that cannot send traffic through public internet except via a dedicated NAT/proxy.
- Reliability & predictability: production latency targets ~ p50 < 200ms for single-turn generation; sustained throughput ~ 400–600 reqs/min during business hours.

Current stack you shared:
- Orchestration: Kubernetes (on-prem), Istio for service mesh
- Auth / KMS: AWS KMS (in some sites), currently evaluating Thales HSM for higher-assurance locations
- Monitoring: Datadog + internal audit pipeline

Success criteria (explicit):
- Data never stored on shared tenant hosts; encryption-at-rest with CMEK; keys under BridgeCare control
- Network topology that allows private peering/VPN + optional air-gap mode
- Audit logs and request-level tracing delivered to BridgeCare log sinks (s3/secure syslog)
- SLA for availability for critical inference endpoints (discuss pricing for dedicated capacity)

Suggested next steps (we propose):
1) Tech deep-dive with your infra/security team — narrow network and key-management constraints (target: Thu Dec 3, 10am ET).
2) Share our private deployment one-pager + preliminary architecture sketch (attached) and a tailored VPC checklist for you to annotate.
3) Red team / security questionnaire — we’ll send our SOC2 and data flow docs; you send any regulatory checklist items we should map.
4) High-level pricing estimate for a private deployment + monthly support + optional on-prem air-gap option (we’ll provide by Dec 7).

Attachments I’m including: a one-page architecture sketch and a VPC readiness checklist you can mark up.

If this looks good I’ll get Monica to scope the questionnaire items and Dev to own the technical deep-dive prep.

Thanks,
Elliot
Elliot Price
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Dana Liu <dana.liu@bridgecarehealth.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karen Hayes <karen.hayes@bridgecarehealth.com>, BridgeCare Tech Ops <techops@bridgecarehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 18:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: BridgeCare discovery — private/VPC deployment playbook (recap & next steps)

Elliot — thanks, this is exactly the level of detail we need. A couple of quick clarifications:
- We do require CMEK for all persisted model artifacts and token caches; HSM-backed keys preferred for the three regulated sites.
- For air-gap sites, we will need a deployable package and clear ops runbook — no outbound internet during updates unless via removable media or a jumpbox.
- On latency: 200ms p50 is a helpful target; we may accept higher cold-starts for batch tasks but prefer consistent interactive latency on live endpoints.

Dec 3 at 10am ET works for the technical deep-dive. I’ll invite our infra lead (Michael Torres) and security manager (Karen).

Please make the checklist editable — we’ll annotate and return.

Dana
Dana Liu
Head of Platform Engineering
BridgeCare Health
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Liu <dana.liu@bridgecarehealth.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:02:00 -0500
Subject: RE: BridgeCare discovery — private/VPC deployment playbook (recap & next steps)

Thanks Dana — noted. A few things we’ll bring to the Dec 3 call and items you can expect from us this week: 

What Redwood will prepare before the call:
- Editable VPC readiness checklist (xlsx) to capture subnet, routing, and firewall rules you’ll need to confirm.
- Private deployment architecture sketch (PDF) showing our peering/VPN, optional air-gap packaging, and where CMEK/HSM sits.
- Short security packet: SOC2 summary, dataflow diagram, and a sample audit-log delivery config (we’ll highlight fields we can provide per-request).

Requests of BridgeCare before the call:
- Network contact + IP ranges for peering/VPN (Michael Torres will do this on the invite).
- KMS/HSM vendor details for the three regulated sites (brand + version) so we validate compatibility.
- A representative prompt set or traffic sample (anonymized) so we can approximate token cost and latency under expected sequences.

Owner assignments:
- Monica: security packet + checklist owner.
- Dev: technical lead on deployment packaging and cold-start mitigation options.
- Elliot: pricing sketch and deal coordination.

We’ve attached the checklist and the sketch — both editable. I’ll add a short comment thread inside the Drive link calling out the fields we need. Looking forward to the Dec 3 deep-dive.

Best,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachments: bridgecare-vpc-checklist.xlsx, redwood-private-arch-sketch.pdf
From: BridgeCare Tech Ops <techops@bridgecarehealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dana Liu <dana.liu@bridgecarehealth.com>, Karen Hayes <karen.hayes@bridgecarehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: BridgeCare discovery — private/VPC deployment playbook (recap & next steps)

Monica / Elliot — thanks for the materials. We reviewed the checklist at a glance and started filling the IP ranges doc (see Drive link). Michael will drop the KMS vendor details into the shared doc by EOD Tue.

A couple of immediate asks for your Dec 3 run:
- Can you include a simple runbook for certificate rotation and key revocation in air-gap mode? That’s a hard requirement for our compliance review.
- Please be ready to show how your private deployment handles model rollbacks and canary traffic splits — we operate a strict change control window.

We’ll see you Thu 12/3 at 10am ET.

— Tech Ops (on behalf of Michael)
